text:
maya: Customer acme-pro (prod) opened a ticket: sudden 5xxs + high tail latency around 10:22 UTC. They say requests were routed to ap-southeast-1 even though their region is eu-west.
alejandro: Do they have auto-fallback enabled?
maya: Yes, their org config is fallback=auto (default). They see a mix of 503 queue_full and occasional 401 invalid_token after spillover.
rachel: 401s could be from hitting a different auth cluster without shared JWKS cache. Can you paste a sample error?
maya: Sample from customer curl repro:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
x-rw-error: queue_full

# later attempts
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
content-type: application/json
{"error":"invalid_token","message":"token not found in jwks for region ap-southeast-1"}
```
juan: I can repro locally by throttling eu-west capacity and enabling fallback. After queue threshold, spillover_count rises and requests start going to ap-southeast-1. Latency jumps from ~30ms to ~250ms.
alejandro: Looking at metrics around 10:20-10:25: eu-west gpu_util hit 98%, queue_length exceeded 500, spillover_count -> 12k in 3m.
alejandro: Routing policy logs show fallback policy executed: route->ap-southeast-1 when queue_len > 100.
rachel: That explains auth mismatch. Our JWKS replication lag meant ap-southeast-1 didn't accept tokens issued by eu-west verifier for a short window.
maya: Customer also flagged billing weirdness — they saw higher per-token cost for those requests. Are we tagging region on billing?
alejandro: Yes we tag actual serving region. So spillover requests billed at the region that served them. I'll flag billing team for reconciliation.
maya: Customer wants immediate mitigation and a follow-up RCA. Short-term options?
rachel: - Disable cross-region fallback for their org (set fallback=reject) OR - increase reserved capacity in eu-west OR - temporarily raise queue threshold to prefer rejecting earlier (avoid cross-region auth issues).
juan: I can flip their org to fallback=reject via admin API; that will return 429/503 instead of spilling to other regions.
alejandro: I'll prepare a routing patch to limit spillover to regions with synced JWKS only. Also adding a guard to annotate spilled requests so billing can be reconciled.
maya: Please run the admin API change and confirm before I tell the customer. Also need repro steps and logs to include in the ticket.
alejandro: Running now — admin call:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer admin-token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://console.redwood.ai/admin/orgs/acme-pro/routing \
  -d '{"fallback_policy":"reject","note":"temp mitigation 2026-03-17"}'
```
alejandro: API returned 200, policy set. I also created a temporary alert: grafana rule "spillover_alert_acme_pro" when queue_len > 100 for 1m.
juan: Adding runbook step to engage infra if spillover_count > 1000 in 5m.
support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1394 — "acme-pro spillover / auth mismatch"; assigned to @alejandro and @rachel.
maya: Thanks team. I'll update the customer: we disabled cross-region fallback for their org to avoid auth mismatches, billing team notified, and we have an RCA in progress on JWKS replication lag + queue threshold tuning.
rachel: Follow-ups: (1) investigate JWKS replication/consistency window; (2) consider tagging spilled requests for billing; (3) evaluate adaptive thresholds per-tenant instead of global.
alejandro: I'll send a short postmortem once we have logs and the billing confirmation.
maya: Customer reply expected: will monitor, asked for ETA on RCA. I'll keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
